$comment: Deployed Barkeep contract addresses on Stellar Testnet.
These are public on-chain identifiers, not secrets: every one of them is
already readable by anyone from the ledger, and they are useless without
the keys that authorise calls. The keys live outside the repository (see
docs/DEPLOYMENTS.md). Checking the ids in is what makes a deployment
reproducible instead of living in one person's shell history.
Testnet only. There is deliberately no mainnet file: per
docs/ARCHITECTURE-v2.md constraint 4, mainnet needs a written policy
AUDIT STATUS: none of these contracts is audited. They are written in
this repository and run on Testnet only. The OpenZeppelin audits cover
the stellar-accounts LIBRARY at v0.7.0-rc.1, four tags behind the 0.7.2
we depend on, and cover none of this code. See ARCHITECTURE-v2.md 4.1.

x402Spike.question: Can an x402 exact payment be made FROM the smart account, authorised by the agent session key under a tab rule, and settled by a facilitator?
x402Spike.answer: Yes with a self-hosted @x402/stellar 2.25.0 facilitator (fee ceiling raised, event check narrowed to the asset contract). No through the public facilitator https://x402.org/facilitator.
x402Spike.note: Seller was a local x402 v2 server on 127.0.0.1; seller payTo and the T0 payer were fresh friendbot accounts with a TAB trustline. Successful flags, ledgers and fees cross-checked on Horizon; T4's auth entry and events read back from RPC.
